chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-A'lawi, from al-Amriki al-Bufaki, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The companions of ships complete their prayer in their ships.
ai.seo_question: Do passengers on a ship shorten their prayers or perform them fully?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the concession of *qasr* (shortening prayers) does not automatically apply to sea travel, as the physical stability and conditions aboard a ship often resemble those of land rather than the severe hardship required to shorten prayers. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle that the permissibility of shortening prayers is contingent upon the actual difficulty of the journey, distinguishing maritime travel from the typical conditions of long-distance land travel.
